chunks: He said: Abul Hasan Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Hubaysh al-Katib reported from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Zafarani, from Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi, from Habib ibn Nasr, from Ahmad ibn Bashir ibn Sulaiman, from Hisham ibn Muhammad, from his father Muhammad ibn al-Saib, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Yamani, from Ikrimah, who said: I heard Abdullah ibn Abbas telling his son Ali ibn Abdillah:

Let knowledge be the treasure you amass; be more jubilant because of that than by the treasure of red gold. For I am entrusting you with words which, if you memorize them, will gather for you the affairs of this world and the hereafter. Do not be among those who hope for the hereafter without deeds, and delay repentance because of long hopes; who speaks about Allah Most High what he does not say about himself; who loves the righteous but does not act with their deeds; who hates the sinners while he is one of them; who fears death but does not hasten to repent. If he falls ill, he spends his time wishing upon Allah Most High; and if he is healthy, he feels safe and is deluded by false hopes. He does not give thanks when given well-being, nor is he patient when afflicted. He rejoices by well-being but does not take lesson from illness. He is amazed by himself when given well-being, and despairs when afflicted. He does not restrain himself from desires nor desist from doubtful matters. He demands much from others' rights but does not demand much from his own rights. He fears for others regarding the slightest of their sins but hopes for himself more than his deeds.

He commands people what he himself does not practice, and forbids them from what he himself does not abstain. He fears the creation regarding other than his Lord, and does not fear his Lord regarding His creation. O my son, the most worthy of people to practice what he says is one who acts by it. And the most deserving of people to fear Allah is he who has sought knowledge. O my son, do not feel secure from the evil of a person until you know what pleases him and what angers him. O my son, consult the scholars and the wise before you resolve upon any matter. O my son, do not argue with a gentle person nor with a fool, for the gentle one will shun you and the fool will harm you. O my son, do not covet what is not yours, and do not despair of what has passed. O my son, know that whoever carries tales to you will carry tales about you, and whoever transfers things to you will transfer about you.

And know that the company of a liar is misery, and the company of a miser is grief, and trust in the fickle is folly. O my son, when you want to befriend a person, then anger him first; if he is just to you in his anger, then accept him, otherwise leave him. O my son, fear Allah Most High and He will protect you from people. And whoever fears Allah, He protects him. And fear Allah with some piety, and make between you and Him a veil. O my son, do not be sweet or you will be swallowed, and do not be bitter or you will be spat out. O my son, the most deserving of people to have no friend is he who deprived friends of good praise upon them and did not preserve the unseen from them. O my son, do not accompany a wicked person or he will teach you his wickedness, and do not disclose your secret to him. And consult in your affairs those who fear Allah Most High. O my son, I have counseled you the counsel of one whom no parent has counseled.

key_terms.التَّوْبَةَ: repentance, returning to Allah from sin
key_terms.الْعِلْمُ: knowledge, the treasure Ibn Abbas advises his son to amass

ai.seo_question: What admonitions did Abdullah ibn Abbas give to his son Ali ibn Abdillah?
ai.summary: Abdullah ibn Abbas delivers a comprehensive set of moral admonitions to his son Ali. He begins by emphasizing that knowledge is more valuable than gold, then describes the contradictions of the hypocrite: one who hopes for the hereafter without deeds, loves the righteous without emulating them, fears death without repenting, and commands others what he himself does not practice. Ibn Abbas then offers practical wisdom: consult scholars before acting, avoid arguing with the gentle or the foolish, test potential friends by seeing how they behave in anger, fear Allah and He will protect you, and maintain moderation — be neither too sweet nor too bitter. He concludes by warning against the company of liars, misers, and the wicked.
